Reviewer-directed fix. trim/collapse/upper, then strip trailing periods and spaces with regex_extract '^(.*?)[.\s]*$' so 'Australia.' structurally reduces to 'AUSTRALIA' before lookup (general rule, not one hardcoded dotted key). map_enum(passthrough=true) maps 'AUSTRALIA'/'AU'/'AUS' -> 'AU' and passes any unlisted letter-only name (ARUBA, SINGAPORE) through unchanged as uppercase text, so genuine foreign countries are neither dropped nor guessed. A final regex_extract '^(\D*)$' returns the value only when it contains no digits, so state+postcode mistypes such as 'WA 6105' become null instead of being emitted as a country; letter-only names are unaffected. 'default: null' is deliberately NOT used, since it would also null real foreign countries.

One Y/blank column per state of operation: one_hot contributes each set column's name, mapped to the state enum. This is the stated service footprint, not the registered address.
Comma-separated ISO3 list of countries the charity says it operates in; split so each value is one observation, keeping the publisher's wording.
Single Y/blank column flagging Public Benevolent Institution status.
Single Y/blank column flagging Health Promotion Charity status; a separate column, so a separate flag rule.

config.notes:
Reviewer feedback addressed: address.country now uses map_enum with passthrough=true (no '__PASSTHROUGH__' sentinel); listed Australian spellings -> 'AU', other countries preserved as uppercase text. entity.status is NOT mapped: no per-row status column and the extract may include revoked charities, so asserting 'active' would be guesswork. entity_type not mapped: suffixes (Incorporated/Ltd/Trust) are name text, not a structured type field. Columns 29-69 are charitable-purpose/beneficiary Y/N flags with no ontology target. Some Other_Organisation_Names values are person-like (e.g. 'Shannon Schedlich'); trading_name confidence kept moderate for that reason. No per-row observation date; fallback to resource last-modified. Address is a business/contact address (Address_Type uniformly 'Business'), so address.full confidence is moderate. One 6-digit Postcode source defect fails validation by design.

[ext-v1] Approved rules 5-9 (address.*) moved to the new establishment role because Address_Type is constant 'Business' (registered premises). ABN is not unique, so establishment key_paths include ABN plus address columns. entity.trading_name is dropped (editable rule 1) because the alias column mixes trading names with former legal names and cannot be classified by evidence; ext.entity.former_name is added in its place, emitting only the 'previously known as' segment. sector_tag uses map_enum over the publisher's purpose wording (scheme acnc_purpose): the acnc_purpose crosswalk op with one_hot produced only raw column names (key_label) or dropped all values (label), so it is not usable here; labels with internal commas were reworded with 'and' to avoid the delimiter lint false positive. Charity_Size has no per-row period, so revenue_band carries scheme only. Remaining forty beneficiary-type Y/N flag columns have no reviewed crosswalk table and are not asserted. Date_Organisation_Established is used only as date_established, never for registration status or validity.

establishment.rationale: Address_Type is constant 'Business' on every row: these columns are the charity's registered business address, i.e. the premises it operates from, not the legal entity.

relationships.rationale: The registered business address is a premises of the charity.

fields.reason: Splitting on ',' and extracting 'previously known as X' can leave the captured group containing stray content such as quotes or the 'previously known as' phrase itself, depending on how the Other_Organisation_Names value is structured. The pattern anchors on the segment end and is acceptable in principle, but none of the held-out records carry an Other_Organisation_Names value with that marker (Walker Close has only an alias, Donnybrook only an alias), so the regex is unexercised and the captured name is not normalised. The rule also has no valid_from/valid_to, which is correct here because the source dates nothing. It is not wrong, but the implementation is unverified.

The address lines are attached to an 'establishment' role, and Address_Type = 'Business' does not distinguish a registered business address from a licensed premises or a contact site; several held-out addresses are PO-box-like or not street addresses ('Community Centre', 'Egan Park'). Treating them as a premises address is a possible premises/entity address confusion. The rule should state explicitly that this is the charity's registered business address, and preferably relax or correct the entity role. The claim that some values are PO boxes is not borne out by the held-out records.

Town_City is mapped to address.locality; it carries case noise ('sunbury', 'DONNYBROOK') and a typo ('Goowa'), but it is emitted as an address locality under the establishment entity role, the same role as rule 1.
The State transform normalises values and maps unknown values to OTHER; the held-out trailing-space value 'SA ' produced 'SA' correctly.

The postcode transform is appropriate for 4-digit Australian postcodes; the stated policy of letting a 6-digit source defect fail validation is an acceptable design choice. The held-out 4-digit values are correct.

The passthrough behaviour is unsafe. 'Austria' is a plausible mistyped or genuine country name and correctly passes through as 'AUSTRIA', but the rule's own logic shows the intended policy is to keep genuine foreign countries; yet the record is an Australian charity with an Australian state and postcode, so emitting address.country = 'AUSTRIA' without qualification publishes a wrong country. Also, passthrough=true means every unlisted letter-only string (including 'NSW', 'TAS', 'VIC' or other state-like garbage) is emitted as a country. If a passthrough free-text country is retained, it should at least be constrained to values not matching an Australian state name, and a state/postcode mismatch should suppress the country rather than assert it.

Charity_Size is the ACNC revenue-size band, so the target fits, but the crosswalk table is marked 'draft - thresholds from ACNC's published size rules; verify the effective date' and the scheme key is 'acnc_size_2022' with no period qualifier. The band scheme is period-dependent in ACNC's rules, and the table is unverified. Emitting scheme acnc_size_2022 without any period evidence, and with blank Charity_Size on two held-out records, is acceptable for a size label, but the unverified table makes the band label status 'doubtful'.

Date_Organisation_Established with dd/MM/yyyy parsing maps correctly to date_established (distinct from registration); the held-out values confirm day-first order (05/09/2023 -> 2023-09-05, 04/08/2023 -> 2023-08-04) and blank -> omitted.
The integer count of responsible persons, including 0, is a valid regulator-reported board size.
Financial_Year_End ('30-Jun', '28-Feb', '31-Dec') matches the dd-Mon pattern and is a reporting-cycle end, not a validity date.
The one_hot of state flags mapped to the operating_region enum is correct; multi-valued rows emit one observation per state, and the stated service footprint is distinct from the address state.
Comma-split ISO3 country values emitted one per observation, preserving the publisher wording. 'AUS' is emitted as-is, which is consistent with 'as the source writes it'.
The Y flag on PBI maps to tax_concession = PBI; held-out record 1 confirms.
The Y flag on HPC maps to tax_concession = HPC; held-out The Transplant Network confirms.

The twelve ACNC purpose flags are decoded to the publisher wording under scheme acnc_purpose, one observation per set flag; the held-out labels match the intended wording and the comma replacement to 'and' does not corrupt the meaning.

missed.reason: When Other_Organisation_Names is an alias or a trading name (for example 'Walker Close Community Centre', 'Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.'), it is a name the entity trades under, and entity.trading_name is the ontology target; the mapping deliberately leaves these unasserted, but they are trading names, not former names.
The column is mapped, but on records where it is blank (held-out records 1 and 5) no band is emitted, which is correct; no additional unmapped column matches this target.
Mapped; there is no gap. Listed only to note that a DGR column, if present in the wider dataset, has no matching mapping.
Already approved and kept unchanged; it is not part of this extension review.
Included in rule 10; held-out Empower Sports Foundation has VIC null and correctly emits every other state.

critic.summary: Most of the extension is sound: date_established, financial_year_end, responsible_persons, operating_region, operating_country, tax_concession, sector_tag and revenue_band fit their targets and roles, multi-valued concepts emit one observation each, and the scheme qualifiers are present. Two problems need attention. Rule 5 is wrong: passthrough of any letter-only value publishes 'AUSTRIA' as the country of an Australian charity at an Australian state and postcode, and it would also pass state names as countries; this needs a state-aware or no-passthrough policy. Rule 1 is doubtful because 'Address_Type = Business' does not establish that this is a premises address (some are venue or site names, some look like contact addresses), and rule 0 is doubtful because the former-name regex is unexercised and does not normalise the capture. The main missed target is entity.trading_name for the alias segments in Other_Organisation_Names, which are left unasserted.

fields.reason: Target is ext.entity.former_name, and the rule correctly disambiguates the ACNC 'Other Organisation Names' field by emitting only comma segments that begin with the 'previously known as' marker, so trading/other names are not mislabelled as former legal names. The held-out non-null values ('Walker Close Community Centre', "Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.") correctly produce no observations because they lack the marker. Quote/punctuation stripping and case-insensitivity are handled, and one observation per segment satisfies the multi-valued target. No valid_from/valid_to is attached, which is appropriate since the source does not date the names. Caveat (not enough to fail): no held-out record contains a positive 'previously known as' example, so the extraction path is unverified; a segment such as 'Previously known as A; previously known as B' would be over-captured as a single name because the split is on commas only.

critic.summary: The single added rule is sound: it maps Other_Organisation_Names to ext.entity.former_name only when a comma segment starts with 'previously known as', which is the correct guard against emitting trading names as former legal names. Held-out records behave as expected (no emissions for marker-less values). The unmapped list is appropriately conservative — Date_Organisation_Established is correctly not used as date_registered, and the Y/N purpose/beneficiary flags, state-operation flags, Charity_Size, Financial_Year_End, PBI/HPC and Operating_Countries have no ontology target. No clearly-matching source column was left unmapped. Only residual risk is the unverified positive extraction path and a semicolon-separated multi-name edge case.
